the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
artificial: made by humans rather than occurring naturally
The garden uses artificial lighting to help plants grow in winter.
intelligence: the ability to learn, understand, and reason well
Artificial intelligence is changing the way many industries operate.
power: electricity or energy supplied to run a device
The whole neighborhood lost power during the storm.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
new: not existing before; recently made, discovered or experienced
They moved into a new apartment near the city centre.
oil: a thick liquid used as fuel, for cooking, or in machines
The mechanic checked the oil before starting the long drive.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
advanced: far ahead in development or progress; sophisticated
The clinic uses advanced equipment to detect illness early.
fabrication: the process of manufacturing something from raw materials
Chip fabrication requires an extremely clean environment.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
global: relating to the whole world; worldwide
Climate change is a global problem requiring international cooperation.
balance: a state in which different things are of equal weight or importance
Finding a balance between work and rest is not always easy.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
century: a period of one hundred years
The tradition has been passed down for more than a century.
access: the means or opportunity to reach, enter, or use something
Every student now has access to a laptop at school.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
rise: to increase, swell, or move upward
Bread dough needs a warm place to rise properly.
fall: a decrease in amount, level, or value
The report records a steady fall in river fish populations.
industrial: The town grew rapidly after a new industrial park opened.
empires: groups of countries or territories ruled by one power
Trade routes once connected empires across Asia and Europe.
wars: periods of armed fighting between countries or groups
Before refrigeration, salt decided which wars a country could afford.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
across: from one side of something to the other
A narrow bridge stretches across the river near the old mill.
secure: The bridge was made secure before traffic was allowed back on.
fields: areas of open land, often used for crops or animals
Golden fields of wheat stretched to the horizon in late summer.
drafted: wrote an early, unfinished version of something
The new policy was drafted by a team of legal experts.
maritime: connected with the sea, ships, or navigation
The country relies heavily on maritime trade routes.
today: on or during this present day
What a body can do today is only part of what it has kept.
however: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something previously said
The plan sounded good; however, it proved too expensive.
profound: very great or intense; showing deep understanding
The loss had a profound effect on the whole community.
shift: to move or change gradually from one state to another
Public opinion began to shift after the documentary aired.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
underway: By the time these dances get underway, daytime transport has largely wound down.
resource: something that can be used to achieve a purpose
Fresh water is becoming a scarce resource in many regions.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
raw: in its natural state; not yet cooked or processed
The factory imports raw cotton before turning it into fabric.
density: the amount of something packed into a given space
The bay has an unusually high density of small limestone islands.
packaged: put into a container or wrapping for sale or storage
The vegetables are washed, packaged and shipped to local stores.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
microscopic: so small it can only be seen with a microscope
The lab identified microscopic traces of the chemical in the water supply.
silicon: a chemical element used to make electronic and computer parts
Silicon is the main material used to make computer chips.
wafers: thin flat discs, especially of silicon used in chips
Chip designs are printed onto thin discs of silicon called wafers.
relies: depends on someone or something for support
The small town relies heavily on tourism during the summer months.
fundamentally: in a basic or essential way
The two theories are fundamentally different in their approach.
upon: on; used to indicate position or timing, especially in formal contexts
The decision rests upon the committee's final vote.
manufactured: made on a large scale using machinery
The parts are manufactured in three different countries.
through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of
Brick, asphalt and concrete absorb heat all day and release it slowly through the night.
extreme: the furthest or most intense point on a scale
Her opinions swing between one extreme and the other.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
manufacturing: the process of making goods on a large scale
Manufacturing jobs declined as more factories became automated.
process: a series of actions taken to achieve a result
Learning a new language is a slow and gradual process.
represents: stands for or acts on behalf of something
This award represents years of dedicated research work.
arguably: used to say a claim is probably true, based on the evidence
This is arguably the most important discovery in the field this decade.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
intricate: The carpet was woven with an intricate pattern of flowers and vines.
technological: relating to technology or its practical use
The factory underwent a major technological upgrade last year.
ever: Nobody can write down rules that nobody ever actually knew.
assembled: fitted together to form a whole
The finished device was carefully assembled by hand in the factory.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
human: relating to or characteristic of people
con người, thuộc về con người
The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
mirrors: phản ánh, là tấm gương của
Good fiction often mirrors the struggles of real life.
polished: made smooth, refined, or perfected through careful effort
Her polished presentation impressed every investor in the boardroom.
measured: found the size, amount, or degree of something
Researchers measured the temperature of the water every hour.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
supply: to provide something that is needed
The factory supplies parts to car makers across the region.
chains: plural of chain; linked sequences of connected parts or events
Several supply chains were disrupted by the port closure.
spanning: extending across or covering an area or period of time
The exhibition features photographs spanning fifty years of history.
four: The table can comfortably seat four people.
continents: the world's main large land masses
Migratory birds travel between continents twice a year.
frontier: the outer limit of knowledge or achievement in a field
biên giới, ranh giới tri thức
Researchers are pushing the frontier of what robots can do.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
engineering: the field of designing and building machines, structures, or systems
She studied engineering before moving into software design.
impossibility: the state of being impossible to do or achieve
Building a perfectly flat map is a geometric impossibility.
now: at the present time; at this moment
Now is a good time to start saving for retirement.
unprecedented: never having happened or existed before
The region experienced unprecedented flooding this year.
subsidies: sums of money given by a government to support an industry
Farmers rely heavily on subsidies during years of low prices.
yet: The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
simply: in an easy or straightforward way; just, merely
She simply smiled and walked away without saying a word.
bonds: certificates issued by governments or companies promising to repay borrowed money with interest
The government issued new bonds to raise money for infrastructure projects.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
talent: a natural ability to do something well
The scout travelled across the country looking for young football talent.
researchers: people who carry out careful study
Researchers have tracked the glacier's retreat for thirty years.
condensed: made thicker or more concentrated by removing water
The recipe calls for a can of condensed milk instead of sugar.
matter: a subject or situation being considered or discussed
Choosing the right career is a matter that deserves careful thought.
software: the programs and instructions used to operate computers
The company develops software for managing hospital records.
architects: people who design buildings and structures
The architects presented three different designs for the new library.
capable: having the ability or skill to do something
The new engine is capable of running on either petrol or ethanol.
distributed: spread out or given to a number of people or places
Food supplies were distributed to families across the flooded region.
training: the process of teaching or practising a skill
Anyone who has stopped training for a year and then started again will recognise the pattern.
specialized: designed or trained for a particular purpose or area of expertise
The lab uses specialized equipment to test water quality.
vendors: people who sell goods, especially in the street
Street vendors line the market during festival season.
strategic: relating to a long-term plan designed to achieve a goal
The port is a strategic location for regional trade.
divergence: The widening productivity divergence between economies reflects disparities in AI adoption.
sự phân kỳ / chênh lệch ngày càng lớn
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
nations: large bodies of people united by common government, history or culture
Delegates from over a hundred nations attended the climate summit.
clusters: groups of things or people gathered closely together
Health officials tracked several new clusters of infection.
those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
digital: using computer technology to store or process information
Most photographs today are stored in digital form rather than on film.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
define: to state the exact meaning or nature of something
Scientists still struggle to define exactly what consciousness is.
coming: moving toward or arriving; originating from a particular source
Cool air keeps coming through the gap under the door.
order: the arrangement of things or events in relation to each other; sequence
Please arrange the files in alphabetical order before filing them.
countries: nations, each with its own government and territory
Trade agreements now link dozens of countries across three continents.
unable: not having the skill, means, or opportunity to do something
Diseases such as polio once left many children unable to walk.
train: to practise or teach a skill regularly; a line of connected railway carriages
The effect is a record of training actually done, not merely intending to train.
models: simplified representations of something, used to explain or predict it
Scientists use climate models to forecast future temperature changes.
domestically: The company now sources most of its materials domestically.
risk: the possibility of something bad or dangerous happening
Investing in a new business always carries some risk.
becoming: The town is becoming a popular spot for young families.
colonies: plural of colony; groups of the same kind of animal living together
Seal colonies gather on the rocky coastline every breeding season.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
cultural: relating to the customs, arts, and social behaviour of a society
The festival celebrates the city's rich cultural heritage.
institutional: relating to a large organisation or established system
thuộc về tổ chức, định chế
The reform requires institutional support from several government departments.
decisions: choices or judgments made after considering options
Difficult decisions about funding are made by the board each year.
elsewhere: in, at, or to another place
If this shop can't help, try looking elsewhere in town.
hegemony: No single superpower can maintain unilateral hegemony over distributed frontier models.
quyền bá chủ, vị thế thống trị
paradigmshift: Generative AI represents a permanent paradigm shift in corporate knowledge synthesis.
autarky: Striving for absolute semiconductor autarky risks catastrophic capital misallocation.
sự tự cung tự cấp tuyệt đối
apparatus: The entire industrial apparatus must adapt to low-carbon computational infrastructure.
bộ máy / thiết bị phức hợp
subsidy: Massive state subsidies were allocated to bolster domestic silicon production.
orchestration: Efficient compute utilization hinges on the seamless orchestration of multi-node clusters.
clientelism: Smaller nations actively resist entering into asymmetric digital clientelism.
tình trạng phụ thuộc / chư hầu
epistemological: Language models embody the epistemological biases inherent in their curated datasets.
thuộc về nhận thức luận / bản chất tri thức
tolerance: Extreme precision optics operate with tolerances tighter than a single atom layer.
dung sai kỹ thuật / độ sai số cho phép
